summary:
North Sulawesi stands under Indonesia's national framework, and the national laws described in the Indonesia record apply to visitors here. No North Sulawesi-specific regulation appears in the sources reviewed.

The mapping of Indonesia's discriminatory regional regulations published by OutRight Action International examined eight provinces and did not include North Sulawesi, so no provincial dress code, curfew or restriction on where transgender people may appear is documented for this province.

Local enforcement has a documented record of harassment during raids. SALUT (Sanubari Sulawesi Utara), the Manado LGBT organisation, reported that police raids in the city have included harassment of LGBT people, including a butch lesbian who was groped during a raid. The account records no arrests or prosecutions.

Official posture has not been uniformly hostile. On 10 November 2012 a waria beach-queen pageant was held at Malalayang beach in Manado, organised by the sitting national legislator Paula Sinjal together with the National Narcotics Agency of North Sulawesi as an outreach event on drugs and HIV/AIDS; Sinjal said waria are part of the local population and deserve attention. No adverse official action was recorded.

Public LGBT organising is visible in Manado. On 11 June 2016 LGBT groups joined the city's women's movement in a street action against sexual violence at Bundaran Zero Point, running from 08.00 to 10.00 WITA, with SALUT taking part.

Visibility carries a social cost. Alexa, elected Ratu Waria Sulawesi Utara for 2016 to 2018 at the Sahid Kawanua Hotel in Manado, said that after taking the title she faced discrimination from sensationalist media and from the public, with her personal crisis peaking around 25 March 2019. No legal or police action appears in her account.

Reporting by victims is limited. SALUT told Suara Kita that victims often do not report because they fear their families will not accept their orientation.
tangentialFactors:
Official engagement and enforcement conduct diverge in Manado. A sitting national legislator and the provincial office of the national narcotics agency sponsored a public trans pageant at a city beach in 2012, while the local LGBT organisation's account of police raids in the same city describes harassment of LGBT people present, including a butch lesbian groped during a raid.

North Sulawesi's documented trans community is organised and public, with an elected province-level pageant title, a pageant sponsored by state bodies and a street action. The recorded harms are social and media-driven rather than legal, and the sources record no prosecution of a trans person in the province.
localsOnly:
SALUT (Sanubari Sulawesi Utara) is the Manado-based LGBT organisation whose director, Coco Jericho, was quoted in the 2016 coverage of the Bundaran Zero Point action. It is the local body that has documented police conduct during raids in the city.

North Sulawesi's trans-women community has a public, elected title, Ratu Waria Sulawesi Utara, conferred at the Sahid Kawanua Hotel in Manado and held by Alexa for 2016 to 2018. The 2012 waria beach-queen pageant at Malalayang beach was staged with the National Narcotics Agency of North Sulawesi as a drugs and HIV/AIDS outreach event.

Residents who are harassed or assaulted often stay silent. SALUT attributes this to fear that families will not accept their orientation, which limits what official complaint data can show.
outOfScopeNotes:
The OutRight Action International mapping of discriminatory regional regulations examined eight provinces and did not include North Sulawesi; the report states its findings are valid for regions beyond its focus set, so the absence of a documented North Sulawesi regulation is not evidence that none exists.

No source in the inventory records a prosecution, arrest or conviction of a trans person in North Sulawesi, and none provides trans-specific violence data for the province. The absence of such records is not evidence that none occurred.

The 2016 Suara Kita account of raid conduct rests on SALUT's testimony and does not name dates, units or outcomes for the raids described.
